properties.name: MEASURED 2026-10-02: a reflow2 built on rocksdb 0.25 (RocksDB 11.8.1) opens 20 of 20 real stores with exports byte-identical to v0.77.0's, and v0.77.0 (RocksDB 10.4.2) opens every store the new engine wrote, including table files the new engine writes in format_version 7, with identical content. The same-crate bump needs no source change, and was taken under the accepted dependency requirement
properties.source: scratchpad rocksdb_compat.py and rocksdb-compat.log, 2026-10-02; reflow2 v0.77.0 release binary; local build of 491a5c9 with rocksdb 0.25
properties.statement:
Evidence for approved-queue item 2(c), the same-crate rocksdb 0.24 → 0.25 bump. Anthony has NOT confirmed that route, and fact:the-dependency-currency-requirement-contradicts-the-agents-md-rocksdb-pin-rule-2026-10-02 says the AGENTS.md rule calls it housekeeping. This records what was measured, not a recommendation. dev_reflow2 hub session, overnight.

THE BUILD. reflow2 origin/main 491a5c9, with only the workspace Cargo.toml line `rocksdb = "0.24"` → `"0.25"` and `cargo update -p rocksdb` (librocksdb-sys 0.17.3+10.4.2 → 0.19.0+11.8.1, plus `rustflags` 0.1.7 added). `cargo build -p reflow2-mcp` compiled with no source change and no warning in 28m42s cold. It is on local branch deps/rocksdb-0-25-same-crate, not pushed. The OLD side was the RELEASED v0.77.0 linux-x86_64 binary, its checksum verified against the release's checksums.txt.

THE CORPUS, 20 stores. Every unheld store under ~/project (18, including one superseded store), plus file copies of the two live-held stores: reflow2's own (6,170 nodes, 39,177 edges, 74 MB) and the dev_reflow2 hub. Each store's identity and meta sidecars were copied with it. The server rendezvous was not copied.

THE METHOD, per store, on four copies of the same bytes (script: scratchpad rocksdb_compat.py):
- a and a2: the old binary exports twice. This is the CONTROL: the export hash is usable only if two old reads agree.
- b: the new binary exports. FORWARD: it must equal a.
- c: the new binary writes one probe ChangeEvent and exports. Then the OLD binary opens c, exports and reads the probe back. ROLLBACK: the two exports must be equal and hold one node more than a.
The harness was validated old-vs-old first. Its first corpus run was refused on 17 stores because the copies lacked the sibling identity file `graph.id.json`, and reflow2 refused rather than minting a new name. Fixed and re-run.

RESULT: control 20/20, forward 20/20, rollback 20/20, probe read back 20/20.

⭐ THE ROLLBACK IS REAL, NOT VACUOUS. Read from each SST footer's format_version field:
- RocksDB 11.8.1 writes block-based table format_version 7 (its OPTIONS file says so). 10.4.2 writes 6.
- Even a read-only open by the new engine leaves v7 tables behind (copy b of reflow2's store: 6 new v7 files).
- On copy c of 3dtictactoe, ALL 7 table files were v7 when v0.77.0 opened it and read every record.
So a user who upgrades and then rolls back to v0.77.0 meets v7 tables, and 10.4.2 reads them.

NOT ESTABLISHED:
- macOS and linux-arm64 builds (only linux-x86_64 measured);
- a release-profile build (debug was measured);
- concurrent shared-server use;
- stores older than those on this machine;
- the flo2.io hosted stores. Untouched by design: the handoff said stop before flo2.io.

═══ LATER, 2026-10-02 — THE ROUTE IS NO LONGER UNCONFIRMED ═══
Carried into reflow2's committed design with the PR that takes the bump (it lived only in the live store until then). Since this was measured, Anthony accepted req:reflow2-keeps-its-dependencies-at-or-near-their-latest-releases ("Yes, accept requirement"), #651 replaced the AGENTS.md rule that called the bump housekeeping, and asked for an order he said "Merge them in the order you suggest", which put this bump after #651. The branch was rebased onto 66620f7 and pushed with that PR.
